items.buying_tips: Check ceiling height, whether it includes a free-weight rack, and the cable ratio; stack versions cost more but change load quickly.
items.safety: Set Smith safeties before every set.
items.keywords: all in one smith cable combo

items.name: Smith attachment for power rack
items.description: A guided-rail bar kit that installs inside a power rack, adding Smith machine work without a separate machine.
items.adjustability: Rails bolt into the rack; bar hooks at many heights.
items.buying_tips: Only buy one made for your exact rack model and height.
items.safety: Recheck the bolts after the first few sessions.

items.name: Technique / training bar
items.description: A light aluminium or steel bar (often 5–10 kg) with full-size sleeves, used for learning lifts and for beginners or youth.
items.buying_tips: Look for a bar that takes 50 mm plates so it can grow with technique and bumper plates. Max load is usually low (~50–100 kg).
items.safety: Respect the low load rating.
items.keywords: technique bar aluminum training youth junior

items.name: Technique plates
items.description: Light plastic or rubber plates at full bumper diameter, so a light bar sits at the right height for learning lifts.
items.buying_tips: Pair with a technique bar for beginners and kids.
items.keywords: technique plates training plastic full diameter

items.name: Tri-grip / handled plates
items.description: Olympic plates with three cut-out hand holes, so they are easier to carry and can be used for plate exercises like front raises and halos.
items.buying_tips: Handled rubber plates double as dumbbell substitutes for many moves.
items.keywords: tri grip handle plate grip plates

items.name: Wall-mounted cable pulley
items.description: A cable column or track bolted straight to a wall stud or masonry, with a stack or plate horn and a sliding pulley. Saves floor space compared with a tower.
items.weight_options: Stack 40–90 kg or plate horn loaded with plates
items.adjustability: Pulley slides on the track; some fold flat.
items.buying_tips: Make sure your wall can take the load; masonry or doubled studs are safest.
items.safety: Anchor into structural framing only.

items.name: Wall-mounted digital cable gym
items.description: A screen on the wall with two motor-driven cable arms that fold out. Motors create the resistance, so weight changes instantly, and it can add eccentric, chain or spotter modes.
items.adjustability: Arms swing and slide to any height; software modes.
items.buying_tips: Needs a subscription for full features and stud or masonry mounting; check max load suits your strength.
items.safety: Use the app or button to cut load if you fail a rep.

items.name: Women's Olympic bar
items.description: A 15 kg, 2.01 m Olympic bar with a thinner 25 mm shaft for smaller hands. Standard in women's weightlifting and good for any lifter with small hands.
items.buying_tips: Bearing sleeves for Olympic lifts; no centre knurl is typical.

items.name: 3D / multi-plane Smith machine
items.description: A Smith machine whose bar carriage also slides forward-back and side-to-side, so the bar path is guided vertically but free horizontally.
items.adjustability: Locks for the horizontal axes on some models.
items.buying_tips: Feels closer to a free bar than a standard Smith; good for gyms whose members fear free weights.
items.safety: Lock the horizontal axes until you are confident controlling the bar.

items.name: Air-resistance cable trainer
items.description: A cable column whose resistance comes from compressed air instead of plates, so load changes by button and speed work is safe.
items.weight_options: Resistance adjusts in ~0.5 kg (1 lb) steps up to ~100 kg
items.buying_tips: Needs an air compressor and is pricey; mostly seen in rehab and sport-performance gyms.

items.name: Competition bumper plates
items.description: IWF-spec calibrated bumper plates with steel hubs, thin profile and colour coding. Used in weightlifting meets and serious clubs.
items.buying_tips: Overkill for most home lifters; good training bumpers suffice.

items.name: Hi-lo pulley station
items.description: Commercial single stack with fixed high and low pulleys (or a short adjustable carriage), often placed at the end of a row of machines.
items.buying_tips: Mainly a commercial purchase; homes are better served by an adjustable tower.

items.name: Jammer / lever arms
items.description: Pivoting plate-loaded arms that attach to a rack, turning it into a press, row or squat machine.
items.buying_tips: Check compatibility with your rack's upright size and hole spacing.

items.name: Lifting platform
items.description: A wood centre with rubber side pads for deadlifts and Olympic lifts. Protects floors and lets you drop bumper plates.
items.buying_tips: A DIY platform of plywood and horse-stall mats is the budget choice.
items.keywords: platform deadlift drop olympic lifting mats

items.name: Multi-station cable jungle
items.description: A large commercial frame with 4–8 weight stacks around it: crossover, lat pulldown, low row and adjustable pulleys, plus a chin-up bar.
items.buying_tips: Commercial only; needs ceiling height and a flat, strong floor.

items.name: Rig
items.description: A long, modular steel frame joining several rack bays, pull-up bars and attachments. Standard in CrossFit and functional gyms.
items.buying_tips: Bolt to the floor or a platform; plan bay widths for barbell work.
items.keywords: rig crossfit functional rig monkey bars

items.name: Treadmill
items.description: A motorised running belt with adjustable speed and usually incline, for walking, jogging and running indoors.
items.adjustability: Speed and incline by console; some folding.
items.buying_tips: Look for a deck of at least 140 x 50 cm for running, a continuous-duty motor of 2.5 HP or more, and a good cushioned deck.
items.safety: Clip on the emergency stop key and straddle the belt when starting.

items.name: Stationary bike
items.description: A seated exercise bike with a flywheel and adjustable resistance, for steady low-impact cardio.
items.adjustability: Seat height and fore-aft; handlebar on some.
items.buying_tips: Magnetic resistance is quieter and needs less upkeep than felt-pad friction.

items.name: Spin bike
items.description: A sturdy indoor cycle with a heavy flywheel, road-bike riding position and resistance knob, for class-style rides and intervals.
items.weight_options: Felt-pad friction or magnetic, flywheel 13–22 kg
items.adjustability: Seat and bar height and fore-aft; resistance knob.
items.buying_tips: Magnetic resistance, an emergency brake and clip-in pedals are worth paying for.
items.safety: Press the resistance knob down to brake; fixed-gear pedals keep spinning.

items.name: Air / assault bike
items.description: A fan bike with moving arm handles: the harder you push and pull, the more resistance the fan gives. Brutal for intervals.
items.buying_tips: Belt-driven models (Echo, AssaultBike Elite) need less upkeep than chain drives.

items.name: Rowing machine
items.description: A sliding-seat erg where you drive with the legs and pull a handle, with fan air resistance. Full body, low impact.
items.buying_tips: The Concept2 RowErg is the gym standard; it holds its resale value and its numbers match everyone else's.

items.name: Elliptical / cross trainer
items.description: A machine with foot pedals that move in an oval path and handles that swing with them, for low-impact full-body cardio.
items.weight_options: Magnetic, 8–25 levels; incline ramp on some
items.adjustability: Resistance, ramp, stride length on some.
items.buying_tips: A stride length of at least 50 cm feels natural for most adults.

items.name: Stair climber
items.description: A machine with a revolving staircase you keep climbing, a very effective low-impact way to work the glutes and lungs.
items.buying_tips: Needs high ceilings and a lot of power; mostly a commercial-gym machine.
items.safety: Hold the rails lightly only; don't lean on them.

items.name: Ski erg
items.description: A standing erg where you pull two handles down from overhead, like double-poling on cross-country skis, for upper-body-led cardio.
items.buying_tips: Needs about 2.3 m of ceiling; the wall-mount version saves floor space.

items.name: Jump rope
items.description: A skipping rope with handles for footwork, coordination and cheap, portable cardio.
items.weight_options: PVC, cable, beaded or weighted; length by height
items.buying_tips: Size it so the handles reach your armpits when you stand on the middle.

items.name: Curved / manual treadmill
items.description: A self-powered treadmill with a curved slat belt; you set the speed by where you run on the curve, ideal for sprints.
items.weight_options: Speed self-set; some add belt resistance levels
items.adjustability: Some have a resistance brake for sled-style pushes.
items.buying_tips: Commercial-grade units are heavy and expensive; try one first as the running feel takes getting used to.
items.safety: Step off to the side rails to stop; the belt keeps moving briefly.

items.name: Open water
items.description: Lakes, the sea or rivers for open-water swimming.
items.buying_tips: A wetsuit and bright tow float make open water warmer and safer.
items.safety: Swim with others in supervised areas and know the conditions.
items.keywords: open water lake sea ocean swim wetsuit

items.name: Running track
items.description: A measured track or flat path for intervals, sprints and tempo runs.
items.buying_tips: Check opening times for school or club tracks.
items.safety: Run counterclockwise and keep the inner lanes free for faster runners.

items.name: Stadium steps
items.description: Long outdoor flights of steps or stadium stands for stair runs, hops and conditioning.
items.safety: Take care on the way down and avoid wet steps.

items.name: Air walker
items.description: A simple frame with two swinging foot pedals that glide forward and back, a very gentle walking-style cardio machine.
items.buying_tips: Very cheap and folds flat, but intensity is limited; also common in outdoor fitness parks.

items.name: Bicycle
items.description: An outdoor bike for rides, commuting and interval work. Pair with a helmet.
items.weight_options: Road, gravel, mountain, hybrid or e-bike
items.adjustability: Saddle and bar height adjust to fit.
items.buying_tips: A proper fit matters more than the price tag; a hybrid suits most fitness riders.
items.safety: Always wear a helmet and use lights in low light.
items.keywords: bicycle bike cycling road mountain helmet

items.name: Bike rollers
items.description: Three drums you ride your own bike on freely, without clamping it, which trains balance and smooth pedalling.
items.weight_options: Free rollers; some add magnetic resistance
items.buying_tips: Start next to a wall or in a doorway until you can balance.
items.safety: Ride beside something you can grab; falls are common at first.

items.name: Bike trainer (turbo)
items.description: A stand that turns your own road or mountain bike into an indoor bike, either by clamping the rear wheel or replacing it (direct drive).
items.weight_options: Fluid, magnetic, fan or smart electromagnetic
items.adjustability: Smart units change resistance by app.
items.buying_tips: Direct-drive smart trainers are quieter and more accurate; check your bike's axle and cassette type.
items.safety: Put a mat underneath and a fan in front; you'll sweat a lot.
items.keywords: turbo trainer smart road bike zwift

items.name: Flat manual treadmill
items.description: A cheap, flat, self-propelled treadmill with a fixed slight incline; you push the belt with your legs, mainly for walking.
items.weight_options: Fixed incline ~5–10°; magnetic tension on some
items.adjustability: Tension knob on some models; folds.
items.buying_tips: Fine for walking without power; most are too short and jerky for running.
items.safety: The belt can feel stiff then lurch; hold the rails when starting.

items.name: Hydraulic rower
items.description: A compact budget rower using one or two hydraulic pistons on swinging arms; cheap and small, but the stroke feels unlike real rowing.
items.buying_tips: Fine for a taste of rowing on a tight budget; pistons get hot and fade on long sessions.

items.name: Magnetic rower
items.description: A quiet rowing machine using magnets for resistance at fixed levels, popular for flats and home use.
items.buying_tips: Cheap models have short rails; if you're over 185 cm check the inseam limit.

items.name: Mini stepper
items.description: A small floor stepper with two short pedals on hydraulic pistons, often with bands for the arms, that fits under a bed.
items.adjustability: Step height dial on some; twist versions.
items.buying_tips: Good for gentle activity in small spaces; not intense enough to replace a full stepper.

items.name: Pedal exerciser
items.description: A small set of pedals with a resistance knob that you use under a desk or chair with your legs, or on a table with your arms.
items.buying_tips: Get one with a strap or rubber feet so it doesn't slide away from your chair.

items.name: Rebounder / mini trampoline
items.description: A small round trampoline for bouncing, jogging and light jumping, gentler on joints than jumping on the floor.
items.weight_options: Springs or bungee cords; 90–130 cm wide
items.buying_tips: Bungee-cord models are quieter and softer than steel springs; a handle bar helps balance.
items.safety: Keep it on a flat floor with clear space around it.

items.name: Running shoes
items.description: Cushioned running shoes for road, treadmill and track running.
items.buying_tips: Get fitted at a running shop and replace shoes every ~500–800 km.

items.name: Swim goggles & cap
items.description: Goggles and a swim cap: the basic kit for lap swimming.
items.buying_tips: Try a few shapes; the best goggle is the one that seals on your face.

items.name: Swim training aids
items.description: Kickboards, pull buoys, fins and paddles that isolate legs or arms or add resistance in the pool.
items.buying_tips: Start with small paddles to protect the shoulders.
items.safety: Build up paddle use gradually.
items.keywords: kickboard pull buoy fins paddles swim

items.name: Under-desk elliptical
items.description: A small pedal-only elliptical you use seated under a desk or chair, for gentle leg movement during the day.
items.buying_tips: Low and quiet; check your desk height leaves enough knee room.

items.name: Walking pad
items.description: A slim, low, often folding treadmill without handrails, mostly for walking at a desk or in small spaces.
items.weight_options: Top speed 6–12 km/h; usually no incline
items.adjustability: Speed by remote or app; folds or slides under a sofa.
items.buying_tips: Check top speed and belt width; most are not built for running even if they claim a running mode.
items.safety: Keep the speed low enough to walk without holding on, as there are usually no rails.

items.name: Cross-country ski machine
items.description: A machine with sliding foot skis and pull cords for the arms, copying classic cross-country skiing for full-body cardio.
items.weight_options: Friction flywheel and arm cord tension
items.adjustability: Leg and arm resistance separately; incline.
items.buying_tips: Mostly second-hand now; takes practice to coordinate arms and legs.

items.name: Incline trainer
items.description: A treadmill built for steep uphill walking, often up to 30–40% incline and some with decline, for hiking-style cardio.
items.weight_options: Incline up to 30–40%; decline to −6% on some
items.adjustability: Speed and steep incline by console.
items.buying_tips: Worth it if you mostly walk; check the incline motor speed and that the deck stays stable at maximum incline.
items.safety: Don't hold the rails at steep inclines; slow down instead.

items.name: Recumbent bike
items.description: A low exercise bike with a backrest and pedals out in front, easy on the back and hips and easy to get on and off.
items.buying_tips: Good for older users, back pain or rehab; check the seat slides far enough for your leg length.

items.name: Smart bike
items.description: A connected indoor bike with automatic, app-controlled resistance, power measurement and often a screen for classes or virtual rides.
items.adjustability: Resistance set by app; fit adjusts to a road bike.
items.buying_tips: Check which apps it works with and whether a subscription is required to use the resistance features.

items.name: Step machine
items.description: A machine with two independent pedals you press down in turn, like climbing stairs without leaving the spot.
items.buying_tips: Look for independent pedals and a solid frame; cheap ones feel bouncy.

items.name: Water rower
items.description: A rowing machine whose resistance comes from paddles in a tank of water, giving a smooth, quiet, boat-like feel.
items.buying_tips: Looks good and stands upright for storage; numbers differ from a Concept2, so don't compare splits.

items.name: Anti-gravity treadmill
items.description: A treadmill inside an air-pressurised chamber that lifts part of your body weight, used in rehab and for low-impact running.
items.adjustability: Air pressure sets how much body weight you carry.
items.buying_tips: Found in physio clinics and pro sports facilities; pay per session rather than buying.
items.safety: Follow your physio's progression plan for body-weight percentage.

items.name: Arc trainer
items.description: An elliptical-like machine with an arc-shaped foot path and high incline, putting more load on the glutes with less knee stress.
items.buying_tips: Mostly found in commercial gyms; try different incline settings to shift work to the glutes.

items.name: BikeErg
items.description: Concept2's fan-resistance indoor bike with the same monitor as their rower, used for comparable, measurable bike work.
items.adjustability: Seat and bar height; road-bike fit.
items.buying_tips: Accepts your own saddle and pedals; very low upkeep compared with friction spin bikes.

items.name: Jacob's ladder
items.description: An endless sloped ladder you climb on all fours; it moves at the speed you climb, for self-paced full-body cardio.
items.adjustability: Speed set by your climbing; hip belt.
items.buying_tips: Mostly seen in CrossFit and military-style gyms; needs a high ceiling.
items.safety: Wear the hip belt so you can't climb off the top.

items.name: Lateral trainer
items.description: An elliptical that adds side-to-side motion to the stride, training the hips and inner and outer thighs.
items.buying_tips: Adds variety for skiers and court athletes; Precor's AMT has a variable stride rather than lateral motion.

items.name: Recumbent cross trainer
items.description: A seated full-body machine where you push foot pedals and move arm handles together, very low impact and used heavily in rehab.
items.adjustability: Seat swivels and slides; arm length adjusts.
items.buying_tips: Common in hospitals, senior centres and physio clinics; good for anyone who struggles to get on a bike.

items.name: Rotating climbing wall
items.description: A rolling climbing wall that turns as you climb so you stay near the floor, for endurance climbing and grip.
items.buying_tips: Rare and expensive; found in climbing gyms and some boutique studios.

items.name: Swim ergometer
items.description: A bench you lie on face down and pull paddles or handles on cords, copying the swim stroke for dryland swim training.
items.buying_tips: Mainly for swimmers and triathletes; long stretch cords are the cheap alternative.

items.name: Swimming pool
items.description: A lap pool for swimming strokes, water running and low-impact rehab work.
items.buying_tips: Check lane-swim times; a pool membership is often bundled with a gym.
items.safety: Never swim alone if you are not a confident swimmer.

items.name: Upper body ergometer
items.description: A table-height hand-cranked bike for the arms, for cardio when the legs can't be used and for shoulder rehab or conditioning.
items.weight_options: Magnetic or air, light to heavy
items.adjustability: Crank height and seat adjust; can work forwards or backwards.
items.buying_tips: Common in physio clinics and adaptive gyms; a pedal exerciser on a table is the cheap home version.
items.keywords: arm bike ergometer ube hand crank

items.name: VersaClimber
items.description: A vertical climbing machine where arms and legs move together on handles and pedals, for very hard full-body, low-impact cardio.
items.weight_options: Hydraulic or air resistance; budget versions use body weight
items.buying_tips: Folding vertical climbers (MaxiClimber) cost far less but are much lighter-duty.

items.name: Calisthenics (bodyweight only)
items.description: Training with nothing but your own body weight and a patch of floor. Covers push-ups, squats, lunges, planks, jumps and skill work.
items.adjustability: Make moves harder with leverage, tempo, range and single-limb variations.
items.buying_tips: Nothing to buy; a mat and a pull-up bar are the most useful first additions.
items.safety: Progress gradually on high-skill moves like handstands and planches.

items.name: Gymnastic rings
items.description: Two free-hanging rings on adjustable straps. They allow dips, rows, push-ups and muscle-ups with a natural, unstable path.
items.weight_options: Wood or plastic rings, 28–32 mm grip, straps 4–5 m
items.adjustability: Strap length adjusts for anything from feet-on-floor rows to full hangs.
items.buying_tips: Wooden rings grip better with chalk; buy straps with numbered markings so both sides match.
items.safety: Master the ring support hold before attempting dips or muscle-ups.

items.name: Parallettes
items.description: Pairs of short, low parallel bars for push-ups, L-sits, planche and handstand work. Come in low (10–15 cm) and high (30–40 cm) versions.
items.weight_options: Low ~10–15 cm, high ~30–40 cm, length 30–60 cm
items.buying_tips: Low parallettes suit planche and push-ups; tall ones allow dips and deeper L-sit and press work.
items.safety: Make sure the feet are wide and non-slip so the bars cannot tip.

items.name: Yoga mat
items.description: A thin, grippy mat for yoga, stretching and floor exercises.
items.buying_tips: 4–5 mm with a grippy top suits most.
items.safety: Clean regularly to keep grip.

items.name: Yoga blocks & strap
items.description: Firm foam or cork blocks (often sold with a strap) that bring the floor closer in yoga poses.
items.buying_tips: Cork is sturdier; foam is lighter.

items.name: Pilates mat
items.description: A thicker, denser mat than a yoga mat for rolling and spinal work in Pilates.
items.buying_tips: Pick 10 mm or more for spine comfort.

items.name: Pilates reformer
items.description: A sliding carriage on springs with straps and a foot bar for resistance Pilates work.
items.adjustability: Change springs, foot bar and strap length.
items.buying_tips: Home reformers fold; studio reformers are sturdier.
items.safety: Check springs are secure before loading the carriage.

items.name: Pilates ring / magic circle
items.description: A flexible ring with pads you squeeze or press for inner thigh, chest and arm work.
items.buying_tips: Dual-pad rings are more comfortable.

items.name: Foam roller
items.description: A firm foam cylinder you roll on to release tight muscles; smooth, textured and vibrating types vary in intensity.
items.buying_tips: A 90 cm medium-density roller suits most; go textured or vibrating later.
items.safety: Avoid rolling directly on joints or the lower back.

items.name: Massage / lacrosse ball
items.description: A firm small ball for pinpointing knots in feet, glutes, shoulders and pecs.
items.buying_tips: A lacrosse ball is cheap and firm; spiky balls are gentler.
items.safety: Move slowly and avoid nerves and bony points.

items.name: Stretching strap
items.description: A non-elastic strap, often with loops, that helps you reach and hold deeper stretches.
items.buying_tips: A looped strap is easier than a plain yoga strap.
items.safety: Ease into stretches; don't yank.

items.name: Dowel / PVC pipe
items.description: A light stick used for shoulder pass-throughs, hip-hinge practice and warm-ups.
items.buying_tips: A broom handle works; PVC is cheap from a hardware store.

items.name: Massage stick
items.description: A handled stick with rolling segments you press along calves, quads and hamstrings.
items.buying_tips: Flexible sticks are kinder on sore legs.

items.name: Meditation cushion
items.description: A firm round cushion (with optional mat) for seated meditation and breathing.
items.buying_tips: Buckwheat filling adjusts height.

items.name: Peanut massage ball
items.description: Two balls joined like a peanut so they straddle the spine for upper-back and neck release.
items.buying_tips: Two lacrosse balls taped together are a free stand-in.

items.name: Small Pilates ball
items.description: A soft, small inflatable ball for squeezing between knees or supporting the back in Pilates.
items.buying_tips: Cheap and versatile.

items.name: Trigger point hook
items.description: A hooked stick that lets you press knots in your own back, neck and shoulders.
items.buying_tips: Pick one with several knobs.

items.name: Yoga blanket
items.description: A dense blanket folded under knees, hips or shoulders for padding and lift.
items.buying_tips: Woollen or cotton blankets fold firmer.

items.name: Yoga strap
items.description: A cotton strap with a buckle that extends your reach in seated and lying yoga stretches.
items.buying_tips: A 2.4 m strap suits most heights.

items.name: Floss band
items.description: A thick latex band wrapped tightly around a joint while you move it, used for mobility.
items.buying_tips: Start with a lighter band.
items.safety: Keep it on no more than 2 minutes; remove if numb.

items.name: Gymnastics grips
items.description: Leather or synthetic palm guards that protect hands and improve grip for high-rep pull-ups, rings and toes-to-bar.
items.buying_tips: Size to your hand; dowel grips suit bars and rings best.

items.name: Percussion massager
items.description: A battery-powered gun that taps the muscles rapidly to ease soreness and warm up.
items.buying_tips: Mid-priced guns are fine; check noise and battery life.
items.safety: Keep it off bones, the neck front and injured areas.

items.name: Scraping tool
items.description: A steel or stone tool scraped along skin and muscles to ease tightness.
items.buying_tips: Stainless steel with smooth edges.
items.safety: Use lotion and avoid broken skin or bruises.

items.name: Yoga bolster
items.description: A firm cylindrical or rectangular cushion that supports the body in restorative poses.
items.buying_tips: Buckwheat or cotton-filled bolsters hold shape.

items.name: Yoga wheel
items.description: A hoop-shaped prop you lie over to open the chest and spine or use for balance.
items.buying_tips: Check the weight rating and padding.
items.safety: Roll slowly and support the neck.

items.name: Aerial yoga hammock
items.description: A fabric sling hung from the ceiling for supported inversions, stretches and aerial yoga.
items.buying_tips: Mount to a beam or rated frame.
items.safety: Check the ceiling mount carefully and start low.

items.name: Crash / gymnastics mat
items.description: Thick folding or crash mats for handstands, levers and landing practice.
items.weight_options: Panel mats ~3–5 cm, crash mats 10–30 cm thick
items.buying_tips: Folding panel mats store flat and suit most home skill work.
items.keywords: crash mat tumbling panel mat gymnastics

items.name: Handstand canes / blocks
items.description: Raised blocks or canes that put the hands above the floor for balance training and handstand presses.
items.buying_tips: A wide, heavy base is essential.
items.safety: Learn to bail safely before training on raised blocks.

items.name: Inversion table
items.description: A table that tips you head-down, held by the ankles, to stretch and decompress the spine.
items.buying_tips: Check the ankle locks and angle stops.
items.safety: Avoid with high blood pressure, glaucoma or heart problems; ask a doctor.

items.name: Monkey bars
items.description: A horizontal overhead ladder for traverses, hangs and grip work; common in parks and ninja gyms.
items.safety: Land with bent knees on a soft surface.

items.name: Pilates tower
items.description: A wall-mounted or reformer-attached frame with springs and a push-through bar.
items.buying_tips: A wall springboard is the home version of a Cadillac.
items.safety: Secure the anchors properly.

items.name: Reformer jumpboard
items.description: A padded board fitted to a reformer for low-impact jumping and cardio.
items.buying_tips: Must match your reformer model.

items.name: Spine corrector
items.description: A small curved barrel with a step for back extension and abdominal work.
items.buying_tips: A foam Pilates arc is lighter and cheaper.

items.name: Stall bars
items.description: A wall-mounted wooden ladder of rungs used for hanging core work, stretching, human flags and assisted strength moves.
items.buying_tips: Mount into studs or masonry; a top pull-up bar extension adds a lot of options.
items.safety: Check the rungs for cracks and the wall fixings for movement.
items.keywords: stall bars swedish ladder wall bars

items.name: Vertical pole
items.description: A sturdy vertical pole fixed floor to ceiling or found outdoors, used for human flags and pole climbing.
items.buying_tips: Fixed poles are steadier than pressure-fit ones for flags.
items.safety: Use a crash mat underneath when learning flags.
items.keywords: pole vertical human flag chinese pole

items.name: Wunda chair
items.description: A box with a sprung pedal you press with hands or feet for demanding Pilates work.
items.adjustability: Spring adjustments; split or single pedal.
items.buying_tips: Split-pedal chairs allow one-sided work.
items.safety: Hold the pedal down until springs settle.

items.name: Climbing rope
items.description: A thick rope hung from the ceiling for rope climbs, legless climbs and grip work.
items.buying_tips: Manila grips well; poly ropes last longer outdoors.
items.safety: Use a mat and climb down hand under hand.

items.name: Cold plunge tub
items.description: A tub of cold water (often chilled) for post-training cold immersion.
items.buying_tips: A stock tank with ice works; chillers add cost.
items.safety: Never plunge alone and avoid if you have heart issues.

items.name: Compression boots
items.description: Inflatable leg sleeves that squeeze in sequence to aid recovery.
items.buying_tips: Common in athletic clubs; home models are pricey.
items.safety: Avoid with blood clots or circulation problems.

items.name: Gymnastics parallel bars
items.description: Long, high parallel bars like gymnastics p-bars for swinging dips, support walks and press work.
items.adjustability: Adjustable height and width on most.
items.safety: Use mats underneath for swinging work.

items.name: Ladder barrel
items.description: A curved barrel next to a ladder for stretching, back extension and side bends.
items.buying_tips: Usually studio kit.

items.name: Peg board
items.description: A wall-mounted board with holes; you climb by moving two pegs up it. A demanding test of pulling and grip strength.
items.safety: Use a mat and move pegs only when the other grip is secure.

items.name: Pilates Cadillac
items.description: A raised table with an overhead frame, springs, a push-through bar and a trapeze for supported Pilates work.
items.buying_tips: Usually studio kit; combination reformer-trapeze units save space.
items.safety: Keep springs controlled and secure.

items.name: Salmon ladder
items.description: A bar moved up a ladder of hooks by explosive pull-ups. Found in ninja and obstacle-course gyms.
items.safety: Master high chest-to-bar pull-ups and use mats before trying it.

items.name: Stretching machine
items.description: A seated station that braces you for supported hamstring, back, chest and hip stretches; leg stretchers spread the legs for splits.
items.buying_tips: Leg stretchers are cheap for splits; full stations are commercial.
items.safety: Use controlled pressure.

items.name: Bulgarian bag
items.description: A crescent-shaped weighted bag with handles, swung and spun around the body for rotational strength.
items.buying_tips: Start light (5–10 kg) because the spin loads the shoulders.
items.safety: Keep a clear radius around you when spinning.

items.name: Indian clubs
items.description: Bottle-shaped clubs swung in patterns to build shoulder mobility, grip and rotational strength.
items.adjustability: Fixed per club; usually bought as a pair.
items.buying_tips: Light wooden clubs suit mobility; steel clubbells suit strength.
items.safety: Start light and swing in a clear area.

items.name: Sledgehammer
items.description: A heavy hammer swung onto a tyre or mat for rotational power and conditioning.
items.weight_options: 4–10 kg (8–20 lb); training hammers have rubber heads
items.adjustability: Fixed; use a lighter or heavier hammer to scale.
items.buying_tips: A shock-absorbing hammer is kinder on your elbows than a builder's sledge.
items.safety: Keep a clear radius around you and strike a tyre that won't bounce it back.

items.name: Farmer's walk handles
items.description: A pair of loadable handles with a central grip used to carry heavy weights in each hand.
items.adjustability: Plate-loaded; some have thicker or rotating handles.
items.buying_tips: Check handle height (pick height) and diameter; pairs are often sold together.
items.safety: Set them down under control at the end, not by dropping them on toes.

items.name: Pulling harness
items.description: A padded harness worn over the shoulders or waist to drag sleds, tyres or vehicles.
items.buying_tips: Look for wide padded straps and a strong D-ring.
items.safety: Check the rope and clips before a heavy pull.

items.name: Arm-over-arm rope pull
items.description: A station or sled you pull towards you hand over hand with a thick rope while seated or braced.
items.adjustability: Machines have adjustable resistance; a sled is adjusted with plates.
items.buying_tips: A thick rope and a sled with an anchor point is the cheap home version.
items.safety: Wear gloves or tape to avoid rope burns.
items.keywords: rope pull truck arm over arm

items.name: Atlas stone
items.description: A round concrete ball lifted from the floor and loaded onto a platform or over a bar.
items.weight_options: 40–200+ kg (90–440 lb); home moulds to cast your own
items.adjustability: Fixed weight; buy a set or cast several sizes from a mould.
items.buying_tips: A mould lets you cast stones cheaply; use tacky and arm sleeves to protect forearms.
items.safety: Lap the stone before extending and keep feet clear when dropping it.

items.name: Axle bar
items.description: A thick (about 5 cm) bar with no rotating sleeves or knurl, used in strongman. Builds grip and makes deadlifts and cleans much harder to hold.
items.buying_tips: Use with a belt-clean style; check the bar holds Olympic plates without slipping.
items.keywords: axle fat bar thick bar strongman apollon

items.name: Car deadlift frame
items.description: A lever frame lifted from long handles, mimicking lifting the back of a car.
items.weight_options: Lever plus plates; up to 400+ kg
items.buying_tips: A trap bar with high handles is the practical home stand-in.
items.safety: Brace hard and keep the lower back neutral.

items.name: Circus dumbbell
items.description: An oversized single dumbbell with a thick, often rotating handle, cleaned and pressed overhead one-handed.
items.buying_tips: A rotating handle is closer to competition spec.
items.safety: Use the free hand to help clean it and keep the wrist stacked.

items.name: Conan's wheel
items.description: A long weighted arm anchored to a central pivot; you hold the end in a Zercher position and walk it around in a circle.
items.adjustability: Plate-loaded arm; fixed pivot bolted to the floor.
items.buying_tips: Needs a lot of floor space and anchoring; mostly a gym or competition piece.
items.safety: Clear the circle before you start walking.

items.name: Fingal's fingers
items.description: A row of hinged poles of increasing weight that you lift from horizontal and push over to the other side.
items.adjustability: Fixed per pole; some home versions are plate-loaded.
items.buying_tips: Rarely sold for home use; look for strongman gyms with one.
items.safety: Walk the pole up in a straight line and step clear when it falls.

items.name: Frame carry
items.description: A rectangular steel frame you stand inside and carry by two long side handles, loaded with plates.
items.adjustability: Fixed; plates on loading posts at each end.
items.buying_tips: Usually a competition piece; check the handle length fits your stride.
items.safety: Keep the frame level and step with short, quick steps.

items.name: Husafell stone
items.description: A flat, awkward stone or steel replica hugged against the chest and carried for distance.
items.adjustability: Fixed; steel versions can be plate-loaded.
items.buying_tips: Plate-loaded steel versions are easier to store and adjust.
items.safety: Lift it close to the body to protect the lower back.

items.name: Keg
items.description: A steel beer keg filled with water or sand and lifted, carried, loaded or tossed.
items.adjustability: Change the weight by adding or removing water or sand.
items.buying_tips: Use an empty keg (not a deposit keg you must return); water sloshes, sand does not.
items.safety: Check the caps are tight so it doesn't leak or burst.

items.name: Power stairs
items.description: A handled weight lifted up a set of steps one step at a time.
items.weight_options: Implement 30–60 kg plus plates; steps ~40 cm
items.buying_tips: Usually a gym piece; a farmer handle and sturdy box can mimic it.
items.safety: Keep the implement swinging between the legs, not into the step.

items.name: Stone platform
items.description: A sturdy platform or set of stepped platforms of fixed heights onto which atlas stones are loaded.
items.adjustability: Some have adjustable heights or a stone ramp to return stones.
items.buying_tips: Pick one with a lip to stop stones rolling off and a height you can adjust.
items.safety: Make sure it can't tip when a heavy stone hits the edge.

items.name: Strongman log
items.description: A thick cylindrical bar with neutral handles cut inside it, cleaned to the chest and pressed overhead.
items.adjustability: Fixed diameter; choose 10 in or 12 in. Handles fixed.
items.buying_tips: Start with a 10 in log; check handle spacing and knurling. Fillable steel logs are cheaper.
items.safety: Clean it with a belly roll and keep the elbows up so it doesn't crush the sternum.

items.name: Strongman shield
items.description: A large, flat steel shield hugged against the chest and carried for distance.
items.buying_tips: Plate-loaded shields let you scale the load.
items.safety: Keep it high on the chest so it doesn't hit your knees.

items.name: Strongman tacky
items.description: A sticky grip paste used on forearms and hands to hold atlas stones and other odd objects.
items.buying_tips: Many gyms ban it; buy one with a remover and check your gym's rules.

items.name: Tyre
items.description: A large truck or tractor tyre flipped end over end, or hit with a sledgehammer, for full-body power and conditioning.
items.adjustability: Fixed; add chains or plates inside to make it heavier.
items.buying_tips: Farm and tyre shops often give used tyres away; choose one you can flip for at least a few reps.
items.safety: Drive with hips and legs, not a rounded back, and never curl it up with straight arms.

items.name: Viking press
items.description: A lever-arm pressing station with two handles at the end, pressed overhead from shoulder height.
items.adjustability: Many have adjustable handle height or swap-in handles.
items.buying_tips: A landmine with a viking handle attachment is the space-saving option.
items.safety: Lock your trunk so you don't over-arch the lower back.

items.name: Yoke
items.description: A tall steel frame with a crossbar that sits across your upper back; you load it with plates and walk with it.
items.adjustability: Fixed frame; many have adjustable crossbar height. Some double as a squat stand.
items.buying_tips: Check crossbar height adjustment and whether it converts to a rack; wide feet reduce wobble.
items.safety: Practise drops and keep the run path clear before loading heavy.

items.name: Boxing gloves
items.description: Padded gloves that protect your hands (and partners) on bags, pads and in sparring.
items.buying_tips: 14–16 oz for general training and sparring; hook-and-loop is easiest solo.
items.safety: Always wrap hands underneath.

items.name: Double-end bag
items.description: A small ball fixed by elastic cords to floor and ceiling that springs back for accuracy and slipping drills.
items.buying_tips: Need solid floor and ceiling anchors; tension changes the speed.
items.safety: Wear light gloves to protect knuckles.

items.name: Focus mitts
items.description: Hand-held padded targets a partner wears so you can drill punch combinations and defence.
items.buying_tips: Curved mitts with good wrist support help the holder.
items.safety: The holder should meet, not push into, the punch.

items.name: Freestanding punching bag
items.description: A punching bag on a base filled with water or sand, so it needs no ceiling mount.
items.weight_options: Base 100–150 kg when filled; 150–180 cm tall
items.buying_tips: Fill the base with sand for less sliding; uppercuts are limited on most models.
items.safety: Put it on a mat so it doesn't creep across the floor.

items.name: Groin guard
items.description: A protective cup or guard worn for kicking sports and sparring.
items.buying_tips: Steel cups are standard for Muay Thai.

items.name: Hand wraps
items.description: Cloth strips wound around the hands and wrists under gloves to support knuckles and wrists.
items.buying_tips: 180 in Mexican-style wraps suit most adults; gel wraps are quicker but less supportive.
items.safety: Wrap firmly across the knuckles but not tight enough to numb fingers.

items.name: Headgear
items.description: Padded headgear worn for sparring to reduce cuts and bruising.
items.buying_tips: Check it doesn't block your vision when you tuck your chin.
items.safety: It reduces cuts, not concussion risk; spar sensibly.

items.name: Kick shield
items.description: A large, thick hand-held pad for full-power kicks, knees and pushes.
items.buying_tips: Curved shields absorb more of the kick for the holder.

items.name: Martial arts mats
items.description: Thick foam mats that cushion falls for grappling, throws and floor work.
items.buying_tips: 4 cm is the minimum for throws; jigsaw mats are fine for drilling.

items.name: MMA gloves
items.description: Thin open-finger gloves that allow grappling as well as striking.
items.buying_tips: 7 oz hybrid gloves are better for sparring than 4 oz fight gloves.
items.safety: They give less protection; go lighter on heavy bags.

items.name: Mouthguard
items.description: A shaped guard over the teeth to protect them and the jaw during sparring and contact.
items.buying_tips: Boil-and-bite is fine to start; custom-fit is worth it for regular sparring.
items.safety: Wear one for any contact sparring.

items.name: Reflex bag
items.description: A ball or pad on a spring-loaded stand (or headband) that rebounds quickly for speed and reaction drills.
items.buying_tips: A weighted base that doesn't tip matters more than the ball.

items.name: Shin guards
items.description: Padded guards covering the shin and instep for kicking pads, bags and sparring partners.
items.buying_tips: Strapped guards with instep protection stay put better.

items.name: Slip bag
items.description: A small weighted ball hung on a rope at head height for practising slipping and head movement.
items.buying_tips: A tennis ball in a sock on a string is a free stand-in.

items.name: Thai pads
items.description: Long forearm-strapped pads a partner holds for kicks, knees, elbows and punches.
items.buying_tips: Curved pads with double straps hold up to kicks.

items.name: Wall bag
items.description: A padded target screwed to the wall for punching where there is no room for a hanging bag.
items.buying_tips: Mount to studs or masonry, not plasterboard.
items.safety: Wrap and glove up; the wall gives no swing.

items.name: Grappling dummy
items.description: A weighted human-shaped bag with limbs for practising throws, takedowns, ground and pound and submissions.
items.buying_tips: A dummy with legs that can be posed suits BJJ; a heavier one suits throws.
items.safety: Throw onto mats only.

items.name: Speed bag
items.description: A small air-filled bag hung from a rebound platform and hit rhythmically for hand speed, timing and shoulder endurance.
items.buying_tips: Buy the platform and bag together; a heavy, stiff platform gives a cleaner rebound.
items.safety: Set the bag at mouth height so you don't strain the shoulders.

items.name: Torso dummy
items.description: A freestanding human-shaped target for accurate strikes to head and body.
items.buying_tips: Fill with sand rather than water for stability.

items.name: Belly pad
items.description: A thick body protector a coach wears so you can land body shots and teeps.
items.buying_tips: Mainly for coaches; check strap adjustment.

items.name: Boxing ring
items.description: A raised, roped (or caged) square for sparring and bouts.
items.buying_tips: A gym fixture; floor rings are cheaper than raised ones.

items.name: Uppercut bag
items.description: A bag shaped or mounted so you can throw uppercuts and hooks at an angle, which a straight heavy bag can't take well.
items.buying_tips: Wall-mounted versions save space.
items.safety: Wrap hands; uppercuts stress the wrists.

items.name: Agility ladder
items.description: A flat flexible ladder laid on the floor for fast footwork patterns, coordination and warm-ups.
items.buying_tips: Flat rungs are less likely to trip you; tape on the floor works if you have none.

items.name: Agility rings
items.description: Flat plastic rings that link into patterns on the floor for hopping and footwork drills.
items.buying_tips: More flexible layouts than a ladder; good for kids' sessions.

items.name: Beaded jump rope
items.description: A rope made of plastic segments on a cord; its weight and feedback make it good for learning and for freestyle tricks.
items.buying_tips: Best rope for beginners and kids; durable outdoors.

items.name: Cones
items.description: Plastic cones or flat disc markers for laying out sprints, shuttle runs and change-of-direction drills.
items.weight_options: Disc 5 cm, cones 15–45 cm; sets of 10–50
items.buying_tips: Disc cones stack and travel easily; taller cones are easier to see in a big space.

items.name: Cordless jump rope
items.description: Two handles with short weighted tethers and no rope, for skipping motion where ceilings or space are too small.
items.buying_tips: Good for low ceilings and flats; doesn't train timing like a real rope.

items.name: Hurdles
items.description: Small plastic speed hurdles (15–30 cm) or adjustable hurdles for hops, bounds and stepping drills.
items.adjustability: Adjustable models set height by sliders.
items.buying_tips: Collapsible plastic hurdles are safest because they bend if you clip them.
items.safety: Use hurdles that fall over if you clip them.

items.name: Reaction ball
items.description: A small rubber ball with knobbly sides that bounces unpredictably, for reaction time and hand-eye coordination.
items.buying_tips: Cheap and portable; tennis balls are an easier starting point.

items.name: Sandbell
items.description: A floppy, sand-filled disc bag with no handles that you slam, throw, carry and twist with.
items.buying_tips: Holds its shape poorly, which is the point; good for grip work.

items.name: Slam ball
items.description: A heavy, dead-bounce ball with a thick shell, sand-filled so it doesn't bounce back when you slam it to the floor.
items.buying_tips: Textured shells are easier to grip with sweaty hands; heavy ones double as strongman-style shouldering balls.
items.safety: Slam on rubber flooring, not concrete or wood.

items.name: Slide board
items.description: A long slick board with stop bumpers at each end; you slide side to side in booties, like speed skating.
items.buying_tips: Longer boards are harder; booties must be kept clean to slide well.
items.safety: Wear the booties and keep shoes off the board.

items.name: Speed parachute
items.description: A small parachute clipped to a waist belt that catches air as you sprint, adding resistance that grows with speed.
items.buying_tips: Needs a long open space and doesn't work well in strong wind.

items.name: Speed rope
items.description: A thin coated-cable rope with bearing handles that spins very fast, used for double unders and fast footwork.
items.buying_tips: Bring spare cables; they fray on concrete.
items.safety: A thin cable stings when it hits; wear long socks at first.

items.name: Sprint resistance harness
items.description: A waist belt with a long elastic cord or strap held by a partner or anchor, for resisted sprints, release sprints and agility work.
items.buying_tips: A belt with a quick-release lets the partner let go for overspeed sprints.
items.safety: Check the cord for cracks before every session.

items.name: Weighted jump rope
items.description: A thick or heavy rope, sometimes with weighted handles, that slows the rotation and works the shoulders and grip harder.
items.adjustability: Fixed; some have removable handle weights.
items.buying_tips: 0.5–1 lb ropes are good for learning; heavier ones are for short conditioning blocks.

items.name: Adjustable plyo box
items.description: A steel box or platform whose height adjusts with pins or stacked risers, so one box covers many jump heights.
items.buying_tips: Make sure the pins lock firmly and the top is non-slip.
items.safety: Re-check the pins before every jump session.

items.name: Agility poles
items.description: Upright slalom poles on spiked or weighted bases for weaving, cutting and change-of-direction drills.
items.buying_tips: Spiked bases for grass; weighted bases for indoor or hard floors.

items.name: Drag sled
items.description: A simple flat metal sled with a plate post that you drag with a harness, straps or rope; cheaper and lighter than a push sled.
items.buying_tips: Works on grass or concrete; a car tyre with a rope is the DIY version.

items.name: Medicine ball rebounder
items.description: An angled trampoline net that throws a medicine ball straight back, so you can do throws and catches without a partner or wall.
items.buying_tips: Use a soft medicine ball; hard balls can damage the net.

items.name: Reaction lights
items.description: Wireless light pods that turn on in random or set orders; you sprint or reach to tap them off, for reaction and agility training.
items.buying_tips: Check the app's drill library and whether it needs a subscription.

items.name: Rope medicine ball
items.description: A medicine ball on a rope or strap that you swing and slam into the ground or a wall for rotational power.
items.adjustability: Hold the rope shorter or longer.
items.buying_tips: Needs clear space; a sledgehammer and tyre is a similar alternative.
items.safety: Check nobody is within swinging range.

items.name: Soft plyo box
items.description: A dense foam box, single or stackable, that forgives missed jumps and is safer for high reps and beginners.
items.buying_tips: Look for a heavy foam core and non-slip base; very light boxes slide.

items.name: Wall ball
items.description: A large, soft-shelled medicine ball made to be thrown at a wall target and caught, as in CrossFit wall-ball shots.
items.buying_tips: Double-stitched synthetic leather lasts longest; 35 cm diameter is standard.

items.name: Rope climber machine
items.description: An endless-rope machine you pull hand over hand against adjustable resistance, standing, seated or kneeling.
items.buying_tips: Great grip and back conditioning; a sled with a rope is the low-cost alternative.

items.name: Tank-style sled
items.description: A wheeled push sled with built-in adjustable brake resistance, so it works on any floor with no plates.
items.weight_options: Resistance levels 1–3+ by lever; some magnetic
items.adjustability: Brake lever sets resistance; push and pull.
items.buying_tips: Great for indoor gyms without turf; check the wheel type won't mark your floor.

items.name: Carabiners & cable extenders
items.description: Steel clips and short chains or straps used to swap attachments, shorten or lengthen cables, and link pulleys to anchors.
items.buying_tips: Buy steel load-rated clips, not keyring-style ones.
items.safety: Only use clips rated well above the loads you lift.

items.name: Door anchor
items.description: A padded strap that closes into a door to anchor bands or a suspension trainer at high, middle or low height.
items.adjustability: Move it to the top, hinge side or bottom of the door.
items.buying_tips: Use the hinge side of a door that opens away from you.
items.safety: Lock the door or make sure no one can open it mid-set.

items.name: Loading pin
items.description: A short steel post with a base that holds plates and hangs from a cable or carabiner. The weight for DIY pulleys and also used for grip training.
items.buying_tips: A longer pin holds more plates; choose a 50 mm (Olympic) post.
items.safety: Never stand under a hanging loaded pin.

items.name: Ankle strap / cuff
items.description: A padded cuff with a D-ring that wraps around the ankle (or wrist) so you can clip a cable to your leg for kickbacks, abductions and leg curls.
items.buying_tips: Get a padded, wide strap with a metal D-ring; a pair lets you switch sides quickly.
items.safety: Make sure the Velcro is fully closed before loading.

items.name: Battle rope anchor
items.description: A wall or floor anchor, strap or weighted base that holds the middle of a battle rope in place.
items.weight_options: Wall bracket, floor plate or anchor strap
items.buying_tips: A strap around a rack post or heavy kettlebell works if you can't drill into a wall.

items.name: Cable hip belt
items.description: A padded hip belt with a ring that clips to a low pulley or loading pin, letting you do belt squats, hip-hinge pulls and marches on a cable.
items.buying_tips: A dip belt works too but a wide, padded belt is more comfortable for heavy loads.

items.name: Double / long tricep rope
items.description: Two separate ropes or one extra-long rope on a single clip, letting the hands travel further apart for bigger range on face pulls and extensions.
items.buying_tips: Nice upgrade if standard ropes feel short for your frame.

items.name: EZ cable bar
items.description: A short cambered bar for cable curls and pushdowns that puts the wrists in a slightly angled grip.
items.buying_tips: Good if straight bars bother your wrists.

items.name: Long lat bar
items.description: A long bar (100–120 cm) with bent ends for wide-grip pulldowns and wide rows.
items.adjustability: Fixed; multi-grip versions have extra neutral handles.
items.buying_tips: Knurled grips and a swivel hook help; check it clears your rack or tower frame.
items.keywords: lat bar long bar wide grip

items.name: MAG / neutral-grip bar
items.description: Bars with parallel handles at a fixed width (close, medium or wide), giving a palms-facing grip for pulldowns and rows.
items.weight_options: Close, medium and wide widths; pronated and supinated versions
items.adjustability: Fixed widths; sold singly or as a set.
items.buying_tips: A medium-width neutral bar is the most useful single choice.

items.name: Neck harness
items.description: A head strap with a chain that holds plates or clips to a low cable for neck extensions and flexion.
items.buying_tips: Start very light; neck work needs tiny increments.
items.safety: Use slow controlled reps and never jerk the load.

items.name: Single D-handle
items.description: A one-hand grip on a ring that clips to a cable. The basic attachment for single-arm and two-handle cable work.
items.weight_options: Sold singly or in pairs; metal stirrup or fabric strap types
items.adjustability: Fixed; pro-style grips rotate or angle.
items.buying_tips: Buy a pair; rotating or soft-strap handles are kinder on wrists for flys and laterals.

items.name: Sled harness
items.description: A shoulder or waist harness with a strap or rope that hooks onto a sled, for forward and backward drags and sprints.
items.weight_options: Shoulder or waist belt; straps 2–4 m
items.buying_tips: Waist harnesses suit sprints; shoulder harnesses let you lean into heavy drags.

items.name: Straight cable bar
items.description: A short straight bar (40–50 cm), often with a revolving sleeve, used for pushdowns, cable curls, straight-arm pulldowns and upright rows.
items.buying_tips: A revolving bar turns freely in your hands and feels smoother on curls.

items.name: Tricep rope
items.description: A short thick rope with knotted or capped ends that clips to a cable. Used for pushdowns, face pulls, curls and cable crunches.
items.buying_tips: A longer rope gives more range on face pulls and overhead extensions.

items.name: Tricep V-bar
items.description: A short bar bent into a V that hangs from the cable, so the wrists stay angled during tricep pushdowns.
items.buying_tips: A swivel hook keeps the bar from twisting.

items.name: V-handle / close-grip row handle
items.description: A triangle-shaped handle with two parallel grips close together, used for seated rows and close-grip pulldowns.
items.buying_tips: Pick knurled or rubber grips that do not spin.
items.keywords: v handle double d close grip

items.name: Wide row bar
items.description: A medium-length bar with angled ends designed for wide-grip seated rows, keeping the hands in a semi-pronated grip.
items.buying_tips: Nice-to-have if you do a lot of upper-back rowing; a lat bar can stand in.

items.name: Wall-ball target
items.description: A wall-mounted target or rig attachment marking the standard height (3 m or 2.7 m) for wall-ball shots.
items.adjustability: Height fixed or adjustable on rig mounts.
items.buying_tips: A tape mark on a solid wall works fine at home.

items.name: Chalk
items.description: Magnesium carbonate (block, loose or liquid) that dries the hands for a better grip on bars and handles.
items.buying_tips: Liquid chalk is less messy and allowed in many gyms that ban loose chalk.

items.name: Elbow sleeves
items.description: Neoprene sleeves for the elbows that keep joints warm on heavy pressing and triceps work.

items.name: Knee sleeves
items.description: Neoprene sleeves that keep knees warm and add a little support in squats and Olympic lifts.
items.buying_tips: 7 mm stiff sleeves for powerlifting; 5 mm for CrossFit and Olympic lifting.

items.name: Lifting belt
items.description: A stiff belt worn around the waist to brace against during heavy squats, deadlifts and presses.
items.weight_options: 10 mm or 13 mm leather; nylon/velcro versions
items.buying_tips: A 10 mm single-prong belt suits most lifters; lever belts are quick but size-locked.
items.safety: A belt helps bracing but does not replace it.
items.keywords: lifting belt weight belt powerlifting lever

items.name: Lifting straps
items.description: Cotton, nylon or leather straps that wrap the bar and your wrist, so grip doesn't limit heavy pulls and rows.
items.buying_tips: Lasso straps are versatile; figure-8 for max pulls; hooks are quick.
items.safety: Don't use figure-8 straps for Olympic lifts; you can't bail.
items.keywords: lifting straps hooks figure 8 versa grips

items.name: Weightlifting shoes
items.description: Stiff shoes with a raised heel that help squat depth and stability in Olympic lifts and squats.
items.buying_tips: Flat, firm shoes suit low-bar squats and deadlifts better.

items.name: Wrist wraps
items.description: Elastic wraps with thumb loops that brace the wrist on heavy presses and front-rack positions.
items.buying_tips: 45–60 cm medium stiffness suits most lifters.

items.name: Deadlift jack
items.description: A small lever that lifts a loaded barbell off the floor so plates can slide on and off easily.
items.buying_tips: Mini plate-ramp wedges are a cheaper alternative.
items.keywords: barbell jack deadlift jack plate loading

items.name: Knee wraps
items.description: Long, stiff elastic wraps wound tightly around the knees to store energy and add weight to heavy squats.
items.buying_tips: Only for equipped-style heavy squatting; not for daily training.
items.safety: Wraps cut circulation; remove them between sets.

items.name: Barbell bands & band pegs
items.description: Heavy loop bands anchored to pegs or the rack and looped over the bar ends, to add load at lockout or help (reverse bands) at the bottom.
items.buying_tips: Rack band pegs or a band-peg platform keep bands from slipping.
items.safety: Check bands for nicks; a snapped band whips hard.

items.name: Lifting chains
items.description: Heavy chains hung from the bar sleeves so load increases as you lift (more chain leaves the floor at lockout).
items.buying_tips: Lead chains with collars make adjustments easy.
items.safety: Secure the chains so they do not swing off the sleeves.

items.name: Chair
items.description: A stable, non-rolling chair used as a bench for dips, step-ups, split squats, incline and decline push-ups and stretches.
items.buying_tips: Pick a four-legged chair without wheels; brace it against a wall for extra stability.
items.safety: Never use a swivel or wheeled office chair.

items.name: Door frame
items.description: A solid door frame used for rows, chest and lat stretches, and as a support to hold.
items.buying_tips: Use a frame set in a solid wall, not a flimsy interior trim.
items.safety: Grip the frame itself, not the door, and keep the door wedged open.

items.name: Hill
items.description: A slope of roughly 5–15% grade for hill sprints, hill repeats and incline walks.
items.weight_options: Ideal sprint hill: 30–60 m at 5–10% grade
items.safety: Walk back down to recover; downhill running is hard on the knees.

items.name: Loaded backpack
items.description: A backpack filled with books, water bottles or plates. Used for rucking and as a stand-in weight for squats, push-ups and lunges.
items.adjustability: Change the load by adding or removing items.
items.buying_tips: A pack with a hip belt and padded straps carries heavy loads far better.
items.safety: Pack the weight high and close to your back.

items.name: Open floor space
items.description: A clear patch of floor or ground, the base for bodyweight work, throws, shuttles and agility drills.
items.weight_options: Roughly 2×2 m for floor work; 10–20 m of straight run for shuttles and sprints
items.buying_tips: Clear trip hazards and check the ceiling height before jumping or throwing.
items.safety: Use a non-slip surface for jumps and sprints.

items.name: Outdoor calisthenics park
items.description: Public outdoor stations with pull-up bars at several heights, dip bars, parallel bars, monkey bars and sometimes rings or sit-up benches.
items.buying_tips: Many cities publish maps of free outdoor gyms.
items.safety: Check bar fixings and wet weather grip before dynamic moves.
items.keywords: street workout park outdoor gym bars

items.name: Park bench
items.description: A solid outdoor bench for dips, step-ups, split squats, incline and decline push-ups and hip thrusts.
items.buying_tips: Choose benches bolted to the ground.
items.safety: Watch for wet or slippery surfaces.

items.name: Playground / monkey bars
items.description: Public playground frames with overhead bars for hangs, pull-ups, monkey-bar traverses and knee raises.
items.buying_tips: Go outside busy hours and respect equipment age limits.
items.safety: Check the bars are dry and solid before swinging.
items.keywords: playground monkey bars jungle gym outdoor

items.name: Sofa
items.description: A sofa works as a hip-thrust bench, a heel anchor for Nordic curls and sit-ups, and a prop for the couch stretch.
items.buying_tips: Heavier sofas make better anchors.
items.safety: Pad the knees for Nordics and check the sofa cannot slide.

items.name: Stairs at home
items.description: A flight of household stairs for stair runs and climbs, plus a single step for calf raises and step-ups.
items.buying_tips: Use stairs with a handrail and good lighting.
items.safety: Hold the rail for calf work and slow down on the way down.

items.name: Sturdy table
items.description: A heavy, stable table you can lie under and pull up to for inverted rows, or lean on for incline push-ups.
items.buying_tips: Solid wood or metal tables with legs at the corners are safest.
items.safety: Never row from a table that could tip; test it with a partial pull first.
items.keywords: table row kitchen desk inverted row

items.name: Towel
items.description: A towel doubles as a slider on smooth floors, a grip trainer on a pull-up bar, and a stretching strap.
items.buying_tips: Thick cotton towels grip best on bars; thin ones slide best on floors.
items.safety: Check the towel and bar for wear before hanging from it.

items.name: Wall
items.description: Any solid, clear wall. Used for support, handstands, wall sits, mobility drills and medicine-ball throws.
items.weight_options: Clear wall ~1.5 m wide and ceiling-high for handstands
items.buying_tips: Use a solid masonry wall for throws; plasterboard can crack.
items.safety: Keep the floor in front clear and non-slip for handstand work.

items.name: Water jugs & household weights
items.description: Filled jugs, bottles, paint cans or shopping bags used as improvised dumbbells and kettlebells for light work.
items.weight_options: ~1–10 kg each (a 4 L jug of water is ~4 kg)
items.adjustability: Fill to the weight you need.
items.buying_tips: Jugs with solid handles are easiest to hold; sand weighs more than water for the same size.
items.safety: Make sure lids are tight and handles will not snap.
items.keywords: water jug bottle milk jug household weight

items.name: Trail & hiking kit
items.description: Grippy trail shoes or hiking boots, often with trekking poles, for trail running and hiking.
items.buying_tips: Fit boots with the socks you will hike in; break them in before long walks.
items.safety: Tell someone your route on remote trails.
items.keywords: hiking boots trail shoes trekking poles hike
